Q: Is it still worthy to learn the programming language 'C'? A:

C is still the most widely-used language for OS kernels. It’s also the basis of many other languages, so it will help a lot with understanding C++, Java, C#, etc. Almost all foreign-function interfaces are based on the C library. Executables you’re debugging probably link to the C runtime library.

Q: Comparison between character and unsigned integer in C on X86 vs ARM A:

It's probably more sensible to compare with an actual character constant. Although integer promotions will still happen to both operands of ==, at least they will happen in the same way and you will not be depending on the signedness of your char of the size of your int or unsigned int.

E.g.

if (*argv[1] == '\xcc')

I believe that it is common for ARM compilers to make char unsigned which means that when '\xcc' is promoted to an integer you get the value 0xcc, not 0xffffffcc.

Q: How to build strong fundamentals of programming without using AI A:

You are right, it depends upon yourself and source. For instance, you can use books. Also, AI is also very useful to learn fundamentals, it is really a good teacher though. In my opinion, you should solve the problem first then try to understand it by using AI as a teacher, so your skills in programming will get better step by step. AI is a helper tool not replacement. The learning procedure varies from one person to another as some may use AI to generate ready codes then learn it basically, it is also not bad method if they use it and understand deeply.

Q: Regex match for file and rename + overwrite old file A:

Final solution for this question for people who are interested:

for i in *; do
   #Wildcar check if current file containt (Exemplaar
   if [[ $i == *"(Exemplaar"* ]]
    then
      #Rename the file to the original name (without Exemplaar conflict)
      NewFileName=$(echo "$i" | sed -E -e 's/[ ][(].*[)]//')
      #Remove the original file
      rm $NewFileName;
      #Copy the conflict file as the original file name
      cp -a "$i" $NewFileName;
      #Delete the conflict file
      rm "$i";
      echo "Removed file: $NewFileName with: $i";
    fi
done

I used this code to replace my database conflict files created by dropbox sync with different computers.

Q: Floor of Natural Logarithm A:

You can't build a table with every n in it, but you probably can build a table with the n's for which floor(ln(n)) changes value. Then you can quickly scan that table, linearly or using bisection. I suppose that you have some limit of how large n can be.
